hints: Focus on counting carbons first, propanoic acid has three carbons, so ask which starting material could lose or keep carbons in one step.
Remember that hot, concentrated acidified manganate(VII) cleaves a C=C double bond completely, turning each end into a carbonyl or carboxyl group.
Check what happens when the double bond in but-1-ene is split, one fragment has three carbons and becomes a carboxylic acid while the one-carbon fragment is fully oxidised.
walkthrough:
**Identify the target**

Propanoic acid is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$. It has three carbons with the $\text{-COOH}$ group. We need a starting material that can give this in just one reagent step.

Target:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$$

**Recall vigorous alkene oxidation**

Cold dilute $\text{MnO}_4^-$ gives a diol, but hot concentrated acidified $\text{KMnO}_4$ cleaves the $\text{C=C}$ bond. Each substituted carbon of the double bond becomes a carboxylic acid or ketone, and a $\text{=CH}_2$ end becomes $\text{CO}_2$.

**Apply to but-1-ene**

But-1-ene is $\text{CH}_2=\text{CHCH}_2\text{CH}_3$. Cleavage of the double bond gives two fragments. The $\text{CH}_2=$ end is oxidised to $\text{CO}_2$ and the $\text{=CHCH}_2\text{CH}_3$ end is oxidised to propanoic acid.

Reaction:
$$\text{CH}_2=\text{CHCH}_2\text{CH}_3 \xrightarrow[\text{heat}]{\text{conc. KMnO}_4, \text{H}^+} \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH} + \text{CO}_2$$

**Conclude the choice**

Only but-1-ene gives propanoic acid directly in one vigorous oxidation step. The other options give four-carbon acids, hydroxy acids, or ketones.

options.A: But-1-ene, $\text{CH}_2=\text{CHCH}_2\text{CH}_3$, undergoes oxidative cleavage with hot concentrated acidified $\text{KMnO}_4$. The terminal $\text{CH}_2$ is lost as $\text{CO}_2$ and the remaining three-carbon fragment forms $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$, propanoic acid, in a single reagent step.
options.B: Butanenitrile, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CN}$, hydrolyses with dilute HCl to give butanoic acid, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$. This has four carbons, not three, so it cannot give propanoic acid.
options.C: $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CN}$ is a hydroxynitrile (lactonitrile). Acid hydrolysis gives 2-hydroxypropanoic acid, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)COOH}$, lactic acid, not propanoic acid. Students who only count carbons often pick this trap.
options.D: Propan-2-ol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$, is a secondary alcohol. Oxidation with acidified dichromate gives propanone, $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$, and it cannot be oxidised further to a carboxylic acid because there is no further H on that carbon.
